exposure: 5-tier fetal heart rate pattern classification (cardiotocography levels 1-2, 3, 4, 5)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 114,201 full-term deliveries (84,703 vaginal and 29,498 cesarean) from the 2018 Perinatal Registry Database of the Japan Society of Obstetrics and Gynecology.
finding: Higher 5-tier cardiotocography levels (3, 4, 5) at delivery were significantly associated with increased crude odds of low 1-min and 5-min Apgar scores, indicating the classification's ability to predict severe neonatal asphyxia.
mod_finding: The correlation between higher 5-tier cardiotocography levels and lower Apgar scores showed a similar trend for both vaginal and cesarean deliveries.
